spans.s:
वेध वेध, अस्, m. (fr. rt. व्यध्), penetra-
tion, piercing, breaking through, perforation; punc-
turing, wounding, wound; hole, excavation; the
depth of any excavation, depth (in measurement); a
particular measure or division of time (= 100 Truṭis).
—वेध-मुख्य, अस्, m. a kind of Curcuma, =
कर्चूर; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= कस्तूरी).
—वे-
ध-मुख्यक, अस्, m. zedoary, Curcuma Zerum-
bet (= हरिद्रा, द्राविडक).

वेधक, अस्, आ, or इका, अम्, piercing, perforating,
a piercer or perforator (of gems); sharp; (अस्), m.,
N. of one of the divisions of Naraka; camphor;
(अम्), n. grain, rice in the ear.

वेधन, अम्, n. the act of piercing, perforation;
penetration, excavation; puncturing, pricking; wound-
ing; a thrust; depth (in measurement); (ई), f. an
instrument for piercing an elephant's ear; a small
gimblet (for perforating gems, shells, &c.); an auger,
gimblet, piercing instrument (in general).

वेधनिका, f. a sharp-pointed perforating instru-
ment (used especially for piercing jewels or shells),
an auger, awl, gimblet, &c.

वेधनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, capable of being pierced,
penetrable, vulnerable.

वेधित, अस्, आ, अम्, pierced, perforated, pene-
trated.

वेधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, piercing, stabbing, perforating;
hitting (a mark); (इनी), f. a leech.
—वेधि-त्व, अम्,
n. capacity of piercing.

वेध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be pierced or perforated;
(अम्), n. a mark for shooting at, butt, target.

वेधस् वेधस्, आस्, आस्, अस् (according to
Uṇādi-s.

. fr. वेध् substituted for वि-धा),
arranging, creating; wise, learned (= मेधाविन्,
Naigh.

); (आस्), m. an arranger, disposer,
creator, (कु-वेधस्, आस्, m. ‘evil creator,’ evil des-
tiny); N. of Brahmā; of Viṣṇu; of Śiva; of the
Sun; of Soma; a wise or learned man; a priest; a
poet, Vedic Ṛṣi.
—वेधस्-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
most wise, wisest, (Sāy. = अतिशयेन मेधाविन्.)

वेधस, अम्, n. the part of the hand under the
root of the thumb (considered as sacred to Brahmā,
see तीर्थ); (अस्), m., N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi (said to
belong to the family of Aṅgiras).

वेधस्या, f., Ved. a desire of performing sacri-
fices, (Sāy. = याग-विधानेच्छा.)
